Deconvolve runs using frozen HRFs learned from other runs

Source: R/crossrun_hrf.R
deconvolve_crossrun_hrf.Rd

Deconvolve runs using frozen HRFs learned from other runs

Usage

deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(
  bold,
  hrf_fit,
  lambda = NULL,
  scaling = "zscore",
  penalty = c("diff2", "diff1", "ridge", "matern1", "sobolev"),
  backend = c("cpp", "r", "wiener"),
  batch_size = 2048L,
  tail_padding = 0L,
  ridge_floor = 1e-08,
  operator_cache_mb = 128,
  nuisance_mode = NULL,
  observation_mask = NULL,
  lambda_grid = 10^seq(-2, 1, length.out = 16),
  gcv_rule = c("min", "1se"),
  lambda_mode = c("auto", "global", "stratified"),
  max_lambda_strata = 4L,
  rwls = "auto",
  highpass = NULL,
  noise_pcs = "auto",
  max_noise_pcs = 10L,
  noise_pool = NULL
)

Arguments

bold

Either a "medusa_nifti_ts" object from read_nifti_ts or named time-by-voxel run matrices with IDs/order/dimensions matching the HRF fit. These should be the same preprocessed BOLD used for estimation.

hrf_fit

Object returned by estimate_crossrun_hrf().

lambda

Nonnegative regularization strength (either a scalar or a per-voxel numeric vector of length ncol(bold[[1]])). If NULL (the default for modern ar1/calibrated fits), selected automatically from lambda_grid by gain-calibrated, task-weighted adaptive prewhitened generalized cross-validation using gcv_rule and lambda_mode.

scaling

Input scaling: zscore (default), noise_sd, demean, none, or psc.

penalty

Quadratic penalty: diff2, diff1, ridge, matern1, or sobolev.

backend

Fixed linear inverse backend: cpp, r, or scalar wiener.

batch_size

Maximum voxel columns per scaling/multiplication block.

tail_padding

Number of appended zero BOLD observations, default zero. Use nrow(hrf_fit$kernels) to reproduce the current voxelwise wrapper assumption.

ridge_floor

Numerical diagonal ridge for cpp/r.

operator_cache_mb

Maximum inverse-operator cache size in MiB, default 128. Zero disables reuse across runs. A single operator may exceed the cache budget while it is being applied, but is not retained in the cache.

nuisance_mode

Nuisance handling for intercept, linear trend, DCT highpass drift (highpass), and supplied nuisance columns: "preproject" (default on modern AR/calibrated fits with cpp or r backends; observation-weighted orthogonal residualization before applying the continuous inverse operator), "joint" (simultaneous unpenalized nuisance normal equations), or "ignore" (default on legacy OLS or wiener fits).

observation_mask

Use fit's valid_rows in the inverse (fit), or all observations (all). Defaults to fit for AR/calibrated, all for OLS/legacy.

lambda_grid

Candidate regularization values evaluated when lambda = NULL.

gcv_rule

Selection rule ("min" or "1se") used when lambda = NULL.

lambda_mode

Spatial regularization tuning mode when lambda = NULL: "auto" (default; stratifies lambda across out-of-sample task-informativeness tiers when the map exhibits SNR heterogeneity across active and background cortex, and falls back to "global" on homogeneous maps), "global" (single scalar lambda for all voxels), or "stratified" (monotone SNR-tier lambda up to max_lambda_strata strata).

max_lambda_strata

Maximum number of SNR regularization strata when lambda = NULL and lambda_mode is "auto" or "stratified" (default 4L).

rwls

Robust weighted least-squares frame weighting mode for transient temporal artifacts (e.g., sub-censoring-threshold motion glitches or RF spikes): "auto" (default; enables "woodbury" on modern AR/calibrated fits and falls back to "none" on legacy OLS or backend = "wiener"), "none" (or FALSE; unweighted GLS), "woodbury" (or TRUE; additive-transient Sparse Bayesian Learning Woodbury covariance \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{AR}} + \mathrm{diag}(\delta^2)\)), or "innovation" (Diedrichsen-style innovation-space downweighting).

highpass

Optional DCT highpass cutoff period in seconds inherited from hrf_fit$settings$highpass when NULL (128 s in modern mode; Inf / disabled when Inf or <= 0).

noise_pcs

Cross-validated GLMdenoise-style background noise-pool temporal PCs: "auto" (default; inherits hrf_fit$specification$noise_pcs when already estimated in Step 1, or extracts \(0 \dots \code{max_noise_pcs}\) PCs on modern fits), 0L/FALSE/"none" (disabled), or a fixed positive integer count.

max_noise_pcs

Maximum candidate noise-pool PCs evaluated when noise_pcs = "auto" (default 10L).

noise_pool

Optional explicit background noise-pool specification (logical mask, integer column indices, or character voxel IDs). Overrides Step-1 noise pool when supplied.

Value

An S3 list of class "crossrun_decon" with activity matrices, per-run scaling/status tables (including per-voxel lambda), the hrf_fit, frozen inverse settings (including scalar reference settings$lambda, the named per-voxel penalty vector settings$lambda_by_voxel ready for 1-line 3D NIfTI export via write_nifti_ts, and SNR tier summary table settings$lambda_strata when stratified), standardized noise_innovations, cached uncensored bold_obs (for \(\le 16{,}384\) voxels) or compact \(m_r \times 64\) whitened_sketch factors (above \(16{,}384\) voxels, enabling bold-free Stage-3 "poet_covreg" shared-error estimation without retaining full 4D BOLD arrays), per-run observation frame_weights, and optional NIfTI voxel_map and geometry metadata (enabling direct write_nifti_ts export without an external reference file). Activity matrices retain voxel IDs and carry tr, time_offset, and observation_mask attributes for subsequent event alignment.

Details

One inverse operator is constructed per selected HRF/noise/lambda stratum and run length, cached for consecutive runs with identical masks/nuisance designs, and applied using block matrix products for cpp/r. Scalar Wiener uses direct block FFT fits. HRFs are frozen; no voxelwise factorization or R fitting loop is required. AR/calibrated fits use a masked GLS inverse with the frozen run-specific noise covariance. A gap of d acquisitions uses rho^d and the corresponding accumulated innovation variance. Censored rows contribute no observations; latent activity is still estimated on the complete original grid. Its observation_mask attribute identifies modeled versus observed samples. Nonfinite/constant signals on usable observations remain NA. Nonfinite censored observations do not invalidate a run. Joint nuisance fitting avoids projecting only the BOLD and inadvertently changing the task model. Wiener requires OLS, nuisance_mode = "ignore", observation_mask = "all". Scaling is applied once before optional padding, and its centers/divisors are returned. Different run z-scores do not preserve absolute between-run units.
